stories.headline: Core industries grow 10.9% in October, led by iron ore, coal and power
stories.summary: Output of India's nine core industries rose 10.9% from a year earlier in October, up from a revised 8.2% in September. Iron ore (26.4%), coal (23.1%), electricity (21.6%) and cement (15.4%) led, while fertiliser, natural gas and crude oil output fell.
stories.why_it_matters: Core industries make up a large part of industrial output, so a strong October points to solid factory growth for the quarter.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (citing provisional Commerce Ministry data).

image.alt: An excavator working on a large coal stockpile

impact.why: Faster growth in coal, power, steel and cement signals stronger industrial activity.
Strong demand data supports metals, cement and power stocks.

stories.headline: SEBI to propose cutting foreign investor sign-up to as little as five days
stories.summary: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said a consultation paper will soon propose simpler rules for foreign portfolio investors, aiming to cut onboarding to as little as five business days. From December 1, KYC reviews for eligible FPIs move to two- and eight-year cycles. He said India's market value is above $5 trillion and 235 companies have raised about ₹1.5 lakh crore through IPOs this financial year.

impact.why: Easier entry for foreign funds can add to inflows into Indian shares.

stories.headline: Russia strikes Kyiv bridges and power plants; Ukraine says 8 killed
stories.summary: Russian missiles and drones hit three bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv overnight and cut power in Kyiv and 10 regions as nuclear plants reduced output. Ukraine's prime minister said 8 people were killed, 6 in Kyiv, and 28 wounded. Russia says it targeted bridges used to move military equipment, after Ukraine partly destroyed the Kerch Bridge earlier this week.
stories.why_it_matters: The escalation comes as US envoys push peace talks, making a quick deal look harder.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera, reporting with Reuters. Casualty figures are from Ukraine's government.

image.alt: Smoke rises over Kyiv's skyline at night during a Russian missile attack

stories.headline: Update: EU and UK seal reset deal on food trade, carbon and youth mobility
stories.summary: New since midday: the deal is done. The UK and EU agreed to cut checks on food, plant and animal goods (worth £5.1 billion to Britain, the UK says), link their carbon markets so goods like steel avoid each other's border carbon levies, and let 100,000 young people a year live and work on each side for up to three years. Legal steps in each country are still to come.
stories.note: The £5.1 billion and 0.5% growth figures are UK government estimates.

impact.why: Easier trade with the EU is a small plus for Britain's economy and the pound.

stories.headline: US military widens Iran blockade to ships taking cargo via ship-to-ship transfers
stories.summary: US Central Command says vessels that receive Iranian-loaded cargo through ship-to-ship transfers may be treated as breaking the blockade, even outside Iranian waters, and can be stopped, boarded or seized. Iran's IRGC says the US cannot enforce its blockade and warned it would hit harder if its ships are attacked.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera. CENTCOM advisory issued Wednesday; claims by each side not independently confirmed.

impact.why: A tighter blockade raises the risk of clashes at sea, adding a small risk premium.

stories.headline: Rupee closes at 92.67, a seven-month high, on a fifth straight day of gains
stories.summary: The rupee settled at 92.67 to the dollar (provisional), up about 65 paise on the day and its fifth gain in a row, after foreign funds kept buying Indian shares and crude oil eased. Business Standard says the rupee is up about 2.5% in November, set for its best month in eight years. Dealers see it trading between 92.40 and 93 next.
stories.why_it_matters: A stronger rupee lowers the cost of oil and other imports but trims exporters' rupee earnings.
stories.note: Close of 92.67 confirmed by All India Radio and PTI; AIR gives the gain as 62 paise, PTI as 65 paise. New since midday: the closing level.

impact.why: Steady foreign buying of Indian shares and softer oil keep lifting the rupee.
A firmer rupee slightly lowers IT exporters' rupee earnings.

stories.headline: India's forex reserves drop $14.2 billion to $705.3 billion
stories.summary: RBI data show reserves fell by about $14.2 billion in the week to November 13 to $705.34 billion, reversing the previous week's rise. Foreign currency assets fell about $7.9 billion and the value of gold holdings dropped $6.18 billion to $98.61 billion as gold prices slid.

impact.why: Reserves are still large, but the drop trims the RBI's cushion to steady the rupee.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 898 points, Nifty ends at 25,801 as India defies Asia's AI rout
stories.summary: The Sensex closed up 898 points (1.1%) at 83,919.71 and the Nifty rose 286 points to 25,800.60, a second straight gain of over 1%, even as Japan's and Korea's markets fell more than 5% on AI fears. Banks led: Kotak Mahindra Bank and HDFC Bank rose over 3%, while Titan and Tata Steel fell 1.7%. Smaller stocks lagged, with more shares falling than rising on the BSE.
stories.why_it_matters: Money leaving AI-heavy Asian markets is flowing into Indian shares, lifting banks and the rupee together.
stories.note: New since midday: closing levels. Asian market falls from Al Jazeera.

image.alt: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai (file photo)

impact.why: Heavy foreign buying lifted the benchmarks over 1% for a second day.
Private banks led the rally, with Kotak and HDFC Bank up over 3%.

stories.headline: Wall Street opens split: Nasdaq falls over 1% as chip stocks slide, Dow edges up
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell about 1.4% at Friday's open and the S&P 500 slipped, while the Dow rose slightly; by about 10:15 am New York time the Nasdaq was down 1.25%, the S&P 500 down 0.3% and the Dow up 0.7%. Chipmakers fell before the bell, with TSMC down about 5%, AMD 4% and Nvidia 2%, and Anthropic's shares slid again on their second day. Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX, hit about 31, its highest since March.
stories.why_it_matters: A deeper US tech sell-off could hit Indian IT stocks and global risk appetite on Monday.
stories.note: Opening levels differ slightly between sources; 10:15 am levels from Yahoo Finance.

impact.why: Doubts over AI spending keep pushing chip and tech shares lower.
Weak US tech can weigh on Indian IT shares.

stories.headline: Update: gold heads for worst week since March; Indian gold down 4.4% in a day
stories.summary: New since morning: Indian bullion rates fell sharply, with 24-carat gold down about 4.4% to ₹1,23,893 per 10 grams and silver down 4.9% to ₹1,52,528 a kg (IBJA). Gold futures traded near $3,570 an ounce, set for their steepest weekly fall since March, as traders priced in a likely US rate rise in December.
stories.note: Indian rates are IBJA closing rates via All India Radio; the dollar price is COMEX futures.

impact.why: Bets on another US rate hike make non-yielding gold less attractive.
Silver is falling even faster than gold.

stories.headline: Brent eases to about $91, heading for a third weekly fall as Hormuz flows recover
stories.summary: Brent crude was down 0.7% at $91.31 a barrel at 14:14 GMT and is on track for a near 5% weekly drop, its third in a row. Reuters says shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are back near pre-war levels, raising talk of a surplus, though near-daily tanker attacks still add a risk premium.

impact.why: Recovering Gulf exports point to more supply than buyers need.
Cheaper oil lowers India's import bill.

stories.headline: India launches its first home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry
stories.summary: ICAR's National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal has developed India's first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan dedicated it to the nation on Friday.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio. No details yet on approvals or rollout.

stories.headline: Titagarh delivers diving support craft DSC A21 to the Indian Navy
stories.summary: Kolkata's Titagarh Rail Systems handed over DSC A21, a locally designed and built diving support craft, at the Naval Dockyard in Mumbai. It carries modern diving gear and will support underwater inspection, salvage and coastal work.

impact.why: A completed Navy delivery adds to its shipbuilding track record.
